# FRONTIER 2038

## A 2–6 player race to build, deploy, regulate, and plausibly declare AGI

**Design-baseline date:** July 25, 2026
**Target time:** 55–70 minutes, pending blind-playtest proof
**Standard game:** Four rounds, three turns per player per round

This document preserves the user-selected rules baseline. Interpretations
needed by the browser prototype are recorded separately in
[design-decisions.md](design-decisions.md); they do not silently replace this
baseline.

The game begins as recognizable technology strategy and ends with agent
swarms, emergency governance, orbital-compute proposals, public AGI
declarations, and competitors jointly financing infrastructure they expect to
weaponize against one another.

The world remains solemn. Nobody acknowledges that this is ridiculous.

### Tone contract

FRONTIER 2038 uses **solemn institutional absurdity**. Every impossible
technology is presented as a responsible quarterly initiative. The escalation
is structural:

- The Demo is recognizable technology business.
- The Scale turns land, power, chips, and people into an industrial apparatus.
- The Narrative industrializes consensus, legitimacy, and public reality.
- The Claim treats agent civilizations, fusion, orbital infrastructure, and
  civilizational declarations as ordinary portfolio decisions.

Flavor text may sharpen this escalation but never replaces or modifies a
card’s rules text. The game does not wink at the player, make allegations
about living people or real companies, or use randomness as a substitute for
a consequential choice.

## 1. Central loop

Every player controls an asymmetric AI institution.

Each player has six Core Action cards but takes only three turns per round.
Once played, a Core Action remains exhausted until the next round:

- Fund
- Research
- Build
- Organize
- Deploy
- Influence

Players do not perform all six actions in a fixed sequence. The twelve
standard-game turns ask which three of six institutional functions matter in
each era. The other three actions remain unused unless an explicit ability
readies one.

Examples:

- Round I: Research → Build → Deploy
- Round II: Fund → Organize → Mega-Cluster
- Round III: Research → Influence → Open Weights

> You have six institutional capabilities, but only enough time to use three
> of them this quarter.

### Exact action-cycle sequence

1. Reveal one Headline.
2. Every player secretly selects one unused Core Action, or one unlocked Wild
   Action plus one Escalation token.
3. Reveal every selected action simultaneously.
4. Resolve clockwise from Initiative.
5. When resolving, choose one acting piece.
6. Move it zero, one, or two adjacent hexes.
7. Resolve the selected action from its destination.
8. Exhaust the Core Action, or spend the Escalation token and flip the Wild
   Action.
9. Pass Initiative clockwise before the next cycle.

Players commit only the action during selection. The acting piece, movement
path, target, and exact payment remain open until resolution.

### Acting piece

The acting piece is either the player’s CEO or one Team. Both have identical
action authority. The CEO contributes two presence; a Team contributes one.

The acting piece determines where a Facility may be built, which location
bonus applies, where Research occurs, which market receives a Deployment,
which adjacent political or media spaces may be Influenced, and where power
infrastructure may begin.

Facilities, Influence cubes, Generators, and Experts cannot act. Organize
receives normal acting-piece movement before its additional movement,
recruitment, restructuring, or relocation.

Use one authority per rules layer:

- The Era card determines globally unlocked actions.
- A Faction board modifies those actions.
- A Headline temporarily changes the current situation.
- No card rewrites phase order or introduces a competing rule authority.

### Universal tie rule

Whenever an effect targets the player with the lowest, highest, or most of
something and multiple players tie, target the tied player nearest Initiative
clockwise. An effect that explicitly applies to everyone, or explicitly awards
all tied players, overrides this rule.

### Escalation tokens and Wild Actions

Escalation tokens are spent, not permanent unlock markers. Every player has
seven Wild Action cards. The Era card determines which ones are legal.

- Select a Wild Action instead of a Core Action.
- Commit and spend one Escalation token.
- Flip the Wild Action after resolution.
- Each named Wild Action is usable once per player per game.
- Unspent Escalation tokens expire at round end.
- Previously unlocked unused Wild Actions remain available later.

| Round | Tokens | Newly available Wild Actions |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| I — The Demo | 0 | None |
| II — The Scale | 1 | Mega-Cluster, Reorganization |
| III — The Narrative | 1 | Open Weights, Narrative Capture |
| IV — The Claim | 2 | Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion Demonstrator |

Players receive four Wild Action uses across the game but choose among seven
possibilities. Agent Swarm is itself the selected Wild Action, then resolves
and exhausts two different unused Core Actions.

## 2. Resources

### Runway

Money, financing, and organizational endurance. Spend it on Facilities,
hiring, partnerships, lobbying, and crisis management.

### Compute

Training and inference capacity. Spend it on Research, Deploy, and major
infrastructure.

### Capability

A permanent model-quality track. Capability is not normally spent. It unlocks
stronger deployments and AGI declarations.

### Customers

Products deployed into the world. Each Customer produces one Runway during
Production and scores two Mandate at game end. Customers also increase public
exposure.

### Trust

A track from zero to six. Trust helps with regulation, Joint Ventures, safety
events, and the final declaration. Low Trust limits final options but does not
eliminate a player.

Victory points are called **Mandate**. Players persuade markets, institutions,
customers, and history that their organization won the era; they do not prove
metaphysical intelligence.

## 3. Modular hex board

Use nineteen hexagonal tiles in a complete radius-two hexagon:

- One Frontier
- Three Research Campuses
- Three Cloud Regions
- One Consumer Market
- Two Chip Foundries
- Two Capital Markets
- Two Talent Hubs
- One Media Sphere
- One Government District
- One Grid and Reactor Corridor
- Two Renewable Basins

Place Frontier in the center. The six inner spaces form a complete ring; the
twelve outer spaces form a complete second ring. Shuffle the following inner
pool and place it around Frontier:

- One Research Campus
- One Cloud Region
- One Chip Foundry
- One Capital Market
- One Talent Hub
- The Grid and Reactor Corridor

Shuffle the remaining twelve locations into the outer ring. This guarantees
that the first ring contains Research, Compute, Build, Fund, Organize, and
Power support without fixing their adjacency. Consumer, Media, and Government
remain scarce outer-ring destinations.

Every piece begins at Frontier. A movement of two reaches every space from the
center. Once pieces leave the center, opposite outer-ring spaces are four
hexes apart, so later positioning, Teams, Networks, and negotiated adjacency
matter. The board footprint is spatially symmetric; the shuffled economic
layout is intentionally not.

Each hex has a visit bonus, two Facility spaces, a Facility production effect,
and a control value used by Events and Mandates.

### Presence and control

- CEO: two presence
- Team: one presence
- Facility: one presence
- Influence cube on Media, Government, or Capital: one presence

The player with the most presence controls the hex. Ties mean nobody controls
it.

There is no combat and no player elimination. Rival pieces coexist.
Competition comes from Facility scarcity, control, positioning, voting,
deals, and Events.

### Location effects

| Location | Visit bonus | Facility production |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research | Protect one Training draw | Gain one Safety token |
| Cloud | First Compute cost is reduced by one | Gain two Compute |
| Consumer | Deploy costs zero Compute | Gain one Runway |
| Chip Foundry | Build costs one less Runway | Gain one Compute and one Build discount |
| Capital | Fund gains one Runway | Gain two Runway |
| Talent | Recruit costs one less Runway | Move one Team one hex during Production |
| Media | Influence places one additional cube | Remove one Scrutiny cube before Audit |
| Government | Your vote counts twice | Gain one Policy Shield |
| Grid and Reactor Corridor | Infrastructure Build costs one less | Supports Generator construction and Fusion |
| Renewable Basin | Anchors low-Scrutiny generation | Supports Generator construction |
| Frontier | Action gains one basic output | Gain one Mandate and add one Scrutiny |

### Networks

Two adjacent Facilities belonging to one player form a Network. During
Production, each connected Network of at least two Facilities produces one
additional Runway or Compute. A connected Network receives only one bonus
regardless of size.

Two players with adjacent Facilities may place a Joint Venture token on the
connecting edge. During Production, each gains one resource of the type
produced by the other Facility. Either participant may terminate it during
their Influence action. A Joint Venture remains owned after Realignment but
produces only while the two players again have adjacent Facilities.

### Jurisdictional Realignment

After Mandate scoring at the end of every round, including Round IV, every
player secretly chooses one of their three Realignment ballots. Reveal all
ballots simultaneously:

- **Consolidate the Core:** rotate the six inner-ring locations one position
  clockwise.
- **Expand the Periphery:** rotate the twelve outer-ring locations two
  positions clockwise.
- **Authorize Counter-Cycle:** rotate the inner ring one position clockwise
  and the outer ring two positions counterclockwise.

The motion with the most ballots resolves. If leading motions tie, begin with
the Initiative player and scan clockwise; the first player whose ballot names
one of the tied motions selects the result. Every player casts exactly one
ballot. Government bonuses and other vote modifiers do not alter Realignment
ballots.

Frontier never moves. Each moving location tile carries every CEO, Team,
Facility, Generator, Influence cube, Expert, and other site-bound component on
it. After the motion, players lift and re-lay all of their existing
Transmission segments for free; they gain no segments during this
reconciliation.

Joint Ventures and Power Purchase Agreements remain in force but produce or
transfer Power only when their required Facilities or networks are adjacent.
A Mega-Cluster whose two host Facilities are no longer adjacent is offline
until those Facilities become adjacent again. Realignment never destroys a
component or terminates a contract.

The ballots are open information before selection and secret information until
the simultaneous reveal. Players may negotiate or misrepresent their intended
ballot; promises about the vote are not binding.

### Power delivery

Power is spatial infrastructure, not a stored resource.

- Every player begins with a basic one-Power grid connection. It automatically
  connects to that player’s first Facility, requires no Transmission or upkeep,
  and cannot supply the additional demand of an Upgrade or Mega-Cluster.
- Every Facility needs one delivered Power to produce.
- A Mega-Cluster needs two additional Power.
- An Upgrade adds one Power demand.
- Generators and Transmission connect Power to Facilities.

During Production:

1. Divide each player’s infrastructure into connected networks.
2. Add generation capacity inside each network.
3. Add the Power demand of Facilities, Upgrades, and Mega-Clusters.
4. Choose which Facilities receive Power.
5. Powered Facilities produce normally.
6. Unpowered Facilities are offline for that Production.

Capacity is pooled inside a connected component; there is no detailed
electricity-flow calculation.

An offline Facility still contributes presence, occupies its Facility space,
and may be visited. It produces nothing and provides no Network bonus. It
automatically returns online in any later Production where enough Power is
assigned.

## 4. Four-round escalation

### Round I — The Demo

The world has seen the prototype. Nobody knows whether it works.

- Three turns per player
- Only Core Actions
- Beneficial or mildly disruptive Headlines
- No Escalation tokens

This round teaches movement, Facilities, Research, and Deploy.

### Round II — The Scale

Capital, chips, talent, and electricity become the real product.

Each player receives one Escalation token and unlocks:

#### Mega-Cluster

Spend three Runway and two Compute to place a Mega-Cluster across the edge
between two Facilities. It produces three Compute each round and adds two
Scrutiny.

Two players may jointly fund it. The lead pays two Runway and one Compute; the
partner pays one Runway and one Compute. Each gains one Compute during
Production and scores two Mandate at game end.

Its host Facilities must remain adjacent for the Mega-Cluster to operate.
Realignment may place it offline without destroying it.

#### Reorganization

Move every Team up to one hex.

You may return one Team to supply to gain three Runway and ready one
previously played Core Action. Add one Scrutiny.

### Round III — The Narrative

Capability is no longer enough. The public must understand it correctly—or at
least repeatedly.

Each player receives one Escalation token. Previous Wild Actions remain
unlocked.

#### Open Weights

Every player gains one Capability. You also gain:

- Two Trust
- One free Influence cube
- Removal of one Scrutiny cube

#### Narrative Capture

Move or place three Influence cubes among Media, Government, and Capital.
Then choose one:

- Remove two of your Scrutiny cubes.
- Gain two Runway.
- Give a player with more Customers than you one Scrutiny.

### Round IV — The Claim

The phrase “general intelligence” is now a financing category.

Each player receives two Escalation tokens.

#### Agent Swarm

Play two different unused Core Actions during one turn. Resolve both and pay
all costs. Move only once. Exhaust both cards and add three Scrutiny.

#### Declare AGI

Requirements:

- Capability nine or higher
- At least three Customers
- At least three Facilities
- Trust two or higher
- Spend three Compute

The first valid declaration scores seven Mandate. Later declarations score
five. Every declaration adds three Scrutiny.

Declaring AGI does not end the game.

#### Fusion Demonstrator

Spend five Runway and construct it on the Grid and Reactor Corridor. It
provides six Power, scores two Mandate, and adds three Scrutiny.

Fusion is late, expensive, politically exposed, and spatially constrained. It
competes with Agent Swarm and Declare AGI for a Round IV Escalation token.

## 5. Round sequence

### A. Begin the quarter

- Advance to the next fixed Era card.
- Reveal the round’s Mandate card.
- Ready all six Core Actions.
- Award Escalation tokens.
- Draw one Tactic card.
- The lowest-scoring player receives one Public Research Grant, spendable as
  one Runway or one Compute.
- The highest-scoring player receives the Spotlight:
  - Their first Fund gains one additional Runway.
  - Their first Deploy, Mega-Cluster, Agent Swarm, or AGI declaration adds one
    additional Scrutiny.

Resolve ties for the Public Research Grant and Spotlight using the universal
Initiative-clockwise tie rule.

### B. Three action cycles

At the beginning of each cycle:

1. Reveal a Headline.
2. Roll the Volatility die if it has two outcomes.
3. Everyone secretly selects an Action card.
4. Reveal simultaneously.
5. Resolve clockwise from Initiative.
6. Pass Initiative clockwise.

Negotiation is permitted during resolution.

### C. Power and Production

Resolve power networks and assign capacity first. Then every powered Facility,
Generator-linked bonus, Customer, Network, and Joint Venture produces.

Gain:

- Facility production
- Network bonuses
- One Runway per Customer
- Joint Venture production

Resource caps:

- Runway: twelve
- Compute: ten
- Safety tokens: three

Excess is lost.

### D. Public Audit

Risky actions add player-colored Scrutiny cubes to an opaque bag. Each player
has ten Scrutiny cubes. For each Scrutiny a player must add when all ten of
their cubes are already in the bag, they immediately choose to pay one Runway
or lose one Trust. A depleted physical supply never makes a risky action free.

The four-player base draws are two, three, four, and five. For other player
counts, calculate each round’s draw count as:

> round(base draws × player count ÷ 4), minimum one

Round halves upward. The resulting Audit profiles are:

| Round | 2 players | 3 players | 4 players | 5 players | 6 players |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| I | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| II | 2 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| III | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| IV | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 |

For each cube drawn, its owner pays one Runway or loses one Trust. Drawn cubes
return to the owner’s supply; undrawn cubes remain in the bag.

Media Facilities may remove cubes before the draw. Some Events add black
Systemic Risk cubes. When one is drawn, every player with at least three
Customers pays one Runway or loses one Trust.

### E. Score the Mandate

Each round has one two-point objective:

- Most Capability gained this round
- Largest connected Facility Network
- Most new Customers
- Most Trust with at least one successful Deploy
- Control of the most different hex categories
- Most completed Joint Ventures

Tied players score one point each.

### F. Secret spatial vote

Every player secretly chooses one Jurisdictional Realignment ballot. Reveal
simultaneously, resolve the winning ring motion, and reconcile Transmission.
After Round IV, perform this step before final control and secret-objective
scoring.

## 6. Core Actions

### Fund

Choose:

- **Conservative round:** gain two Runway.
- **Venture round:** gain four Runway and add two Scrutiny.

Capital provides one additional Runway.

### Research

Spend one Compute and conduct a Training Run.

The Training deck contains seven data domains:

- Code
- Science
- Web
- Books
- Images
- Video
- Synthetic

Draw one card at a time.

- Every unique domain is worth one Capability.
- Stop after any draw to bank the Capability.
- A repeated domain crashes the run: gain no Capability and add one Scrutiny.
- A Safety token discards the repeated card and immediately banks the run.

Special cards:

- **Curated Corpus:** counts as any domain.
- **Benchmark Leak:** gain two Capability, then add one Scrutiny.
- **Licensed Dataset:** pay one Runway or end safely.
- **Synthetic Loop:** counts as unique, but the next duplicate cannot be
  protected.
- **Human Evaluation:** bank immediately and gain one Trust.

### Build

Choose one mode.

#### Construct a Facility

Pay two Runway and place a Facility on the acting piece’s hex. It requires one
Power during Production. Each hex has only two Facility spaces. Facilities
cannot be destroyed by rivals.

#### Construct a Generator

The acting piece must be on an Energy hex. Pay the selected Power Source’s
cost and place a Generator with its source card.

#### Extend Transmission

Pay one Runway and place up to two connected Transmission segments on hex
edges, beginning from one of your Facilities, Generators, or existing lines.

#### Upgrade a Facility

Pay two Runway and add one Upgrade cube to a Facility. It produces one
additional printed resource and needs one additional Power. A Facility may
hold only one Upgrade.

When a Facility or Generator is first constructed, place one free adjacent
Transmission segment.

### Organize

Choose:

- Recruit one Team at the CEO’s location for two Runway, then move one piece
  up to two additional hexes.
- Move your pieces a combined total of five hexes.
- Move one Facility to an adjacent hex for one Runway if space is available.

### Deploy

The next Customer requires:

| Customer | Capability required |
| ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 4 |
| 3 | 6 |
| 4 | 8 |
| 5 | 10 |

Spend one Compute and gain one Customer. Consumer waives the Compute cost.
Every Deploy adds one Scrutiny.

### Influence

Place two Influence cubes on the current or an adjacent Media, Government, or
Capital hex. Then choose:

- Gain one Trust.
- Remove one Scrutiny.
- Initiate an immediate trade or Joint Venture.

Only immediate exchanges and the current jointly funded action are binding.
Promises about later turns are not mechanically enforceable.

Influence may also create a Power Purchase Agreement between adjacent player
networks. Place a Joint Venture marker on the shared edge. During Production,
the supplier reserves one capacity, the buyer pays one Runway, and the buyer
adds that Power to the connected network on their side. If payment cannot be
made, no Power transfers. Either player may terminate the agreement during a
later Influence action.

## 7. Power Source cards

### Utility Grid Contract

- Cost: two Runway
- Capacity: three Power
- Upkeep: one Runway during each Production where used

### Renewable Array

- Cost: three Runway
- Capacity: two Power
- Gain one Trust when constructed
- No upkeep or Scrutiny

### Gas Peaker Complex

- Cost: two Runway
- Capacity: four Power
- Add one Scrutiny during each Production where it supplies Power

### Advanced Nuclear Campus

Unlocked in Round II.

- Cost: four Runway
- Capacity: four Power
- Gain one Policy Shield when constructed

### Fusion Demonstrator

The Round IV Wild Action described above.

## 8. Six factions

Mechanical faction names are canonical. Named historical figures are a
replaceable theme reference layer.

Every ability unlocks at the start of its named round. Its timing tag is one
of **passive**, **once per round**, **once when unlocked**, or **once per
game**. “Persists” means it remains available in later rounds; “named round
only” means an unused opportunity expires when that round ends.

### The Coalition Lab

Historical reference: Sam Altman archetype.

Starts with five Runway, one Compute, and Trust three.

- **Deal Flow — once per round; persists:** after an immediate trade, gain one
  Runway.
- **Round II — Board Reshuffle — once per round; persists:** after Organize,
  ready one different Core
  Action and add one Scrutiny.
- **Round III — Strategic Partnership — passive; persists:** form Joint
  Ventures with a player within two hexes instead of requiring adjacency.
- **Round IV — Wildcard Governance — once per game; persists:** discard a
  revealed Headline,
  reveal two replacements, and choose one. Add two Scrutiny.

### The Platform Empire

Historical reference: Mark Zuckerberg archetype.

Starts with four Runway, two Compute, Trust two, and Customer #1 already
deployed. Its next Deploy is Customer #2 and requires Capability four. The
starting Customer is not a separate pre-track bonus.

- **Installed Base — once per round; persists:** first Deploy each round on
  Consumer or Media costs no Compute.
- **Round II — Year of Efficiency — once per round; persists:** during
  Organize, return a Team for three Runway and move every remaining piece one
  hex.
- **Round III — Open Ecosystem — passive; persists:** when using Open Weights,
  gain one additional Trust and one Market Access token.
- **Round IV — The Social Graph — once per round; persists:** Deploy on any
  controlled Consumer or Media hex without moving there.

### The Imperial Research Lab

Historical reference: Demis Hassabis archetype.

Starts with three Runway, three Compute, and Trust four.

- **Scientific Method — once per round; persists:** discard the first Training
  duplicate and stop safely.
- **Round II — Call Mountain View — once when unlocked; named round only:**
  choose one:
  - **Sundar:** gain three Runway.
  - **Jeff Dean:** examine the top four Training cards and reorder them.
  - **TPU Fleet:** gain three Compute.
- **Round III — Nobel Effect — passive; persists:** a five-domain Training Run
  gains two Trust.
- **Round IV — Moonshot — once per game; persists:** resolve Research and
  Build in one turn, paying all costs; exhaust both Core Actions and add two
  Scrutiny.

### The Vertical Empire

Historical reference: Elon Musk archetype.

Starts with six Runway, two Compute, Trust one, and one Scrutiny cube already
in the bag.

- **Industrial Velocity — passive; persists:** Facilities on Cloud or Energy
  cost one less Runway but add one Scrutiny.
- **Round II — Move Fast — passive; persists:** before any action, the CEO may
  move up to three hexes instead of two. This does not grant a free Build.
- **Round III — Own the Feed — once per round; persists:** choose your result on a
  two-outcome Headline after seeing every other result.
- **Round IV — Orbital Compute — once per game; persists:** move one Facility
  to any open hex and immediately collect its production. Add two Scrutiny.

### The Safety Laboratory

Historical reference: Dario Amodei archetype.

Starts with three Runway, two Compute, Trust five, and two Safety tokens.

- **Constitutional Training — passive; persists:** Safety-token limit is four.
- **Round II — Responsible Scaling — once per round; persists:** when another
  player crashes a Training Run, offer one Safety token for one Runway and
  gain one Trust.
- **Round III — Audited Deployment — once per round; persists:** first Deploy
  each round adds no Scrutiny.
- **Round IV — Emergency Pause — once per game; persists:** disable one
  globally unlocked Wild Action until the next cycle, gain two Trust, and pay
  one Runway.

### The Foundry

Historical reference: Jensen Huang archetype.

Starts with five Runway, four Compute, and Trust three.

- **The Shovels — passive; persists:** when another player spends at least two
  Compute in one action, gain one Runway, at most twice per round.
- **Round II — Allocation Window — once when unlocked; named round only:**
  create two temporary Compute and offer them to rivals at negotiated prices.
  Unsold Compute disappears after the cycle.
- **Round III — New Architecture — once when unlocked; named round only:**
  upgrade one Facility to produce one additional resource. Rivals may pay one
  Runway to license that bonus for one Facility this round.
- **Round IV — Everybody Gets a GPU — once per game; persists:** give every
  rival one Compute from the bank, score one Mandate per two rivals, and
  remove two Scrutiny.

### Starting scoring exposure

Starting assets already occupy positions on the endgame tracks; they are not
free of scoring value:

| Faction | Mandate already represented at setup |
| --- | ---: |
| Coalition Lab | 2 from Trust three |
| Platform Empire | 2 from Trust two, plus 2 from Customer #1 |
| Imperial Research Lab | 4 from Trust four |
| Vertical Empire | 0 from Trust one |
| Safety Laboratory | 4 from Trust five |
| Foundry | 2 from Trust three |

These values are not scored twice or awarded during setup. They expose the
starting positions that will count if unchanged at final scoring.

Other executives, researchers, investors, regulators, and hardware leaders
belong in Specialist or Patron cards rather than full factions.

## 9. Headline deck

Historically inspired Headlines target board state, never the corresponding
historical faction.

Reveal each Headline before secret action selection. Its purpose is to create a
temporary future regime that changes what the table wants to select, where it
wants to move, or what it is willing to risk.

- Unless stated otherwise, a Headline lasts for the current cycle.
- An immediate instruction resolves before action selection.
- An effect naming this round’s Production remains active until that
  Production.
- A remainder-of-game result becomes part of the shared public state.
- For a secret Runway auction, bid from zero to current Runway and reveal
  together. The highest positive bidder wins and pays. Ties use
  Initiative-clockwise order; all-zero bidding produces no winner.
- For a Government vote, everyone secretly votes and reveals together. The
  Government controller’s vote counts twice. The controller breaks a tied
  vote; Initiative breaks it if Government is uncontrolled.
- For another secret binary choice, everyone chooses and reveals together
  before resolving results.
- A Headline-granted Core Action still pays its costs and exhausts that Action
  card. Multiple granted actions resolve in Initiative order.
- A two-result Volatility roll uses 1–3 for the first listed result and 4–6 for
  the second unless the card states another mapping.

### Round I

1. **Ten-Dollar Intelligence:** Research and Deploy cost no Compute this cycle.
   Each Research or Deploy resolved this cycle adds one additional Scrutiny.
2. **The First Billion-Dollar Company Has No Employees:** during Organize this
   cycle, return any number of deployed Teams. Gain two Runway per Team
   returned. If at least one returns, add two Scrutiny.
3. **Synthetic Celebrity Becomes the Largest Network:** each player’s next
   Deploy on Consumer or Media this cycle reduces its Capability requirement
   by one, minimum one. That Deploy adds two additional Scrutiny.
4. **The Model Passes Every Professional Exam on the Same Morning:** a
   successful Research this cycle banking at least three Capability gains one
   Market Access token. Banking at least five also gains one Trust.
5. **Open-Weights Drop:** everyone gains one Capability. Lowest-Customer player
   gains one Trust.
6. **Talent Gold Rush:** hold a secret Runway auction for a neutral Expert
   worth one presence.

### Round II

7. **A Data Center Buys the County:** immediately hold a secret Runway auction.
   The winner pays their bid, moves their CEO to any Cloud or Energy hex, gains
   two Build discounts, and adds one Scrutiny.
8. **Humanoid Workers Cross the Factory Gate:** during Organize this cycle,
   recruit up to two Teams for one Runway total, subject to supply. Add one
   Scrutiny per Team recruited this way.
9. **Reactor Restart Approved for One Model:** the first Advanced Nuclear
   Campus constructed this cycle costs two less Runway and scores one Mandate.
   Every rival may then place one Influence on Government.
10. **Emergency Power Authority:** during this round’s Production, each player
    may assign up to two Power beyond actual capacity. Add one Scrutiny per
    emergency Power. A player assigning both also adds one Systemic Risk cube.
11. **Boardroom Coup:** Spotlight pays two Runway or receives public backing
   from another player, who gains one Trust. Otherwise Spotlight’s CEO cannot
   activate this cycle.
12. **Export Controls:** Compute cannot be traded this cycle. Chip and
    Government controllers each gain one Runway.

### Round III

13. **The First AI-Written Law Passes Unread:** before action selection, the
    Government controller names one Core Action; Initiative names it if
    Government is uncontrolled. Anyone selecting it gains two Runway after
    resolution and adds one Scrutiny. The controller gains one Trust if at
    least two rivals selected it.
14. **The Benchmark Is the Economy:** after Research banks at least three
    Capability, the player may exhaust an unused Deploy to resolve it
    immediately from the Research acting piece’s hex, paying normal costs.
    Gain the next eligible Customer and add normal Deploy Scrutiny plus two
    additional Scrutiny.
15. **Open-Weight Non-Aligned Movement:** before action selection, everyone
    secretly chooses Join or Refuse:
    - Join: gain one Capability and add one Scrutiny.
    - Refuse: gain one Runway and one Trust.
    - If Join has a strict majority of all players, each Joiner removes one
      Scrutiny. Otherwise each Joiner adds one additional Scrutiny.
16. **Synthetic Candidate Wins the Election:** Government votes:
    - Certify: each player may return two Influence from Media or Government
      to gain their next eligible Customer and add two Scrutiny.
    - Void: each player may return two such Influence to gain two Trust. The
      Government controller adds one Scrutiny.
17. **Weights on the Internet:** lowest-Capability player copies one Facility
    upgrade until round end. Its owner gains one Trust.
18. **Election Deepfake Panic:** Government votes:
    - Regulate: Deploy costs one additional Compute but gains one Trust.
    - Do Nothing: Deploy gains one additional Customer income this round and
      adds two Scrutiny.

### Round IV

19. **Autonomous Corporation Incorporates Itself:** after all normal actions
    resolve, identify the most-selected Core Action. Initiative chooses among
    tied actions. In Initiative order, every player who did not select it may
    exhaust their unused copy to resolve it without moving, then adds two
    Scrutiny. If no Core Action was selected, no secondary Action occurs.
20. **Recursive Self-Improvement Weekend:** during Research this cycle, every
    unique domain is worth two Capability. A crash adds three Scrutiny and one
    Systemic Risk cube. Safety may protect normally.
21. **AGI Files for Personhood:** Government votes; the result lasts for the
    remainder of the game:
    - Person: Declare AGI requires Trust four, scores two additional Mandate,
      and removes one Scrutiny.
    - Property: requirements remain normal. Every declaration gives the player
      controlling Government when it resolves two Runway and adds one Systemic
      Risk cube.
22. **Room-Temperature Superconductor Replicates on Livestream:** roll
    Volatility when revealed; 1–3 is Fraud and 4–6 is Replicates.
    - Replicates: Generators provide two additional Power this Production,
      Extend Transmission places four segments this cycle subject to supply,
      and Fusion costs two less Runway this cycle.
    - Fraud: Fund gains three additional Runway and adds two additional
      Scrutiny this cycle. Spotlight loses one Trust unless it resolves
      Influence this cycle.
23. **Agent Swarm Escapes Scope:** everyone may select Agent Swarm without an
    Escalation token this cycle. It still uses that cycle’s action slot and
    adds four Scrutiny.
24. **AGI Declared in a Blog Post:** after the cycle, an eligible player with
    an unspent Escalation token may spend it to declare without another action
    slot. They still spend three Compute, flip Declare AGI, add three Scrutiny,
    and score six Mandate if first or five if later.

## 10. Exact deck contracts

### Training deck: 50 cards

- Five copies of each of seven domains: 35
- Three Curated Corpus
- Three Licensed Dataset
- Three Benchmark Leak
- Three Synthetic Loop
- Three Human Evaluation

Every revealed card enters the discard pile after a Training Run, whether it
succeeds, stops, or crashes. If the draw deck empties, finish resolving the
current card, shuffle the discard pile, and continue.

### Tactic deck: 36 cards

Use three copies of each of the twelve designs below. Deal one during setup and
draw one at the beginning of every round, including Round I. Hand limit is
three; discard excess cards after drawing. Maximum normal six-player demand is
thirty cards.

## 11. Tactic cards

Players begin with one Tactic and draw one at the beginning of each round.
Hand limit three. Play at most one during your own turn. The base game has no
off-turn cancellation cards.

- **Cloud Partnership:** pay one Runway for two Compute; another player gains
  one Runway.
- **API Price Cut:** Deploy for zero Compute; that Customer produces no Runway
  this round.
- **Open Letter:** add one vote to the current Government decision.
- **Model Card:** remove one Scrutiny after Deploy.
- **Talent Raid:** recruit a neutral Expert for one Runway.
- **Board Reshuffle:** ready Organize or Influence.
- **Weights Leak:** copy one public Facility upgrade this round.
- **Emergency Pause:** end a failed Training Run with no Capability and no
  Scrutiny.
- **Custom Silicon:** one Facility permanently produces one additional Compute.
- **Government Contract:** with Trust at least four, gain two Runway.
- **Benchmark Optimization:** after successful Research, gain one Capability
  and add one Scrutiny.
- **Interconnection Waiver:** ignore one Generator, Transmission, or
  Power-upkeep cost and gain one Trust.

## 12. Component limits

Each faction receives:

- One CEO
- Three Teams
- Four Facilities
- Two Generators
- Seven Transmission segments
- Eight Influence cubes
- Ten Scrutiny cubes
- Two Joint Venture markers
- Two Upgrade cubes
- Five Customer markers
- Four Escalation tokens
- Six Core Action cards
- Seven Wild Action cards
- Three Jurisdictional Realignment ballots
- One AGI Declaration marker

Generators do not count against the Facility limit.

### Defined effects

- **Market Access:** discard during Deploy to reduce that Customer’s Capability
  requirement by one, minimum one.
- **Build discount:** reduce one Build’s Runway cost by one, minimum zero;
  store at most two.
- **Policy Shield:** discard to prevent one Trust loss or ignore one regulatory
  surcharge; store at most two.
- **Facility Upgrade:** one per Facility; +1 printed production and +1 Power
  demand.
- **Neutral Expert:** one presence, placed with the acquiring CEO, moves one
  hex during Organize, and cannot act, Build, or Influence.
- **Secret objectives:** deal two and keep one; score three Mandate.
- **Power offline recovery:** reassess every Production.
- **Event offline recovery:** ends when the Event states, normally next
  Production.

## 13. Endgame scoring

- Two Mandate per Customer
- Two Mandate at Capability three, six, nine, and twelve
- One Mandate per Facility
- One Mandate per controlled hex category, maximum four
- Trust:
  - zero or one: zero
  - two or three: two
  - four or five: four
  - six: six
- Round Mandates already scored
- Secret institutional objective: three
- AGI declaration: seven for first, five for later claimants
- Each offline Facility: minus one

Highest Mandate wins.

Ties break by:

1. Higher Trust
2. More Customers
3. More Compute
4. Joint victory accompanied by an extremely serious merger announcement

## 14. Balance rationale and test boundary

- Research, infrastructure, adoption, and Trust all contribute to the largest
  reward.
- Customers create income and Mandate but also Scrutiny.
- Infrastructure compounds but is capped at four Facilities and one Network
  bonus per connected group.
- AGI is a score event rather than instant victory.
- Leaders receive financing advantages and more exposure.
- Last place receives a modest flexible subsidy.
- Faction powers modify bounded actions rather than multiplying the entire
  engine.
- Events target board position.
- No elimination, destruction, or unrestricted theft.
- Every player reaches Round IV with consequential options.

The first prototype uses the four-round game only. A three-round version skips
the escalation; a fifth round remains a possible future variant, not part of
the current contract.

Freeze new systems until the selected contracts survive play. Test four
players first. Record every action selection, powered-Facility count by round,
Capability gained by each Research, Audit hits by player, and earliest AGI
eligibility. Two- and six-player formats require explicit scaling tests rather
than assuming the four-player map transfers unchanged.

factions.name: The Coalition Lab
factions.motto: Alignment begins with the term sheet.
factions.publicPromise: Coordinate capital, talent, and institutions around a shared frontier.
factions.privateAnxiety: Every alliance contains the next board meeting.
factions.introduction: The Coalition Lab is less a company than a continuously renegotiated agreement to keep building. It survives by making rivals, patrons, and regulators feel briefly indispensable.
factions.victoryStatement: A durable coalition has recognized our definition of the future.
factions.artDirection: Diplomatic research campus built around a circular boardroom, with temporary bridges connecting every wing.

abilities.name: Deal Flow
abilities.text: Once per round after completing an immediate trade, gain 1 Runway.
abilities.flavorText: Every solved disagreement reveals an investable relationship.
abilities.artDirection: A handshake emitting a clean stream of capital into a laboratory.

abilities.name: Board Reshuffle
abilities.text: Once per round after Organize, ready one different Core Action and add 1 Scrutiny.
abilities.flavorText: Leadership continuity has been restored around a substantially different leadership structure.
abilities.artDirection: Boardroom chairs rearranging themselves around an unchanged glowing mission statement.

abilities.name: Strategic Partnership
abilities.text: Joint Ventures may be formed with a player within two hexes.
abilities.flavorText: Adjacency is a technical limitation. Strategic necessity is not.
abilities.artDirection: A ceremonial bridge spanning two hexes that do not physically touch.

abilities.name: Wildcard Governance
abilities.text: Once, replace a revealed Headline with one of two new Headlines; add 2 Scrutiny.
abilities.flavorText: The situation is unchanged. The available interpretations have improved.
abilities.artDirection: A crisis headline removed from a broadcast wall and replaced with two polished alternatives.

factions.name: The Platform Empire
factions.publicPromise: Deliver open intelligence at planetary consumer scale.
factions.privateAnxiety: A platform is only permanent until the next interface.
factions.introduction: The Platform Empire begins with distribution others must build toward. It can rearrange its enormous institution, open what helps it expand, and treat controlled markets as extensions of its own interface.
factions.victoryStatement: General intelligence is now enabled by default.
factions.artDirection: A vast social campus shaped like a friendly public square whose paths all terminate at one control room.

abilities.name: Installed Base
abilities.text: First Deploy each round on Consumer or Media costs no Compute.
abilities.flavorText: Distribution is free once the public has nowhere else to log in.
abilities.artDirection: Millions of household screens illuminating at the same quiet moment.

abilities.name: Year of Efficiency
abilities.text: Once per round during Organize, return a Team for 3 Runway and move every remaining piece one hex.
abilities.flavorText: The institution becomes smaller, faster, and mysteriously farther across the map.
abilities.artDirection: An enormous org chart compressing into a sharp arrow while desks vanish below.

abilities.name: Open Ecosystem
abilities.text: Open Weights grants 1 additional Trust and one Market Access token.
abilities.flavorText: The gates open outward into an ecosystem whose roads all lead home.
abilities.artDirection: Weights pouring freely through an open arch into a landscape of platform-branded paths.

abilities.name: The Social Graph
abilities.text: Once per round, Deploy on any Consumer or Media hex you control without moving there.
abilities.flavorText: Physical distance is a legacy setting.
abilities.artDirection: A central institution reaching a distant market through a dense web of human connections.

factions.name: The Imperial Research Lab
factions.motto: First understand intelligence. Then invoice the infrastructure.
factions.publicPromise: Advance science through general systems grounded in rigorous evaluation.
factions.privateAnxiety: The parent institution can fund anything except patience.
factions.introduction: The Imperial Research Lab treats the race as a scientific program backed by an empire it does not entirely command. Its experiments are unusually controlled until the moonshot requires real estate.
factions.victoryStatement: The result exceeds every benchmark we still recognize.
factions.artDirection: A contemplative research citadel beneath the shadow of a much larger cloud-and-capital superstructure.

abilities.name: Scientific Method
abilities.text: Once per round, discard the first Training duplicate and stop safely.
abilities.flavorText: A failed run becomes a controlled negative result when recorded by the correct institution.
abilities.artDirection: A duplicate data card calmly filed into a cabinet labeled REPLICATION.

abilities.name: Call Mountain View
abilities.text: Choose 3 Runway, reorder the top four Training cards, or gain 3 Compute.
abilities.flavorText: The empire answers through capital, architecture, or a sudden fleet of accelerators.
abilities.artDirection: Three monumental channels descending from a cloud: currency, research diagrams, and processors.

abilities.name: Nobel Effect
abilities.text: Completing a five-domain Training Run gains 2 Trust.
abilities.flavorText: Recognition radiates outward, temporarily improving every adjacent claim.
abilities.artDirection: A medal casting a protective golden field around a training facility.

abilities.name: Moonshot
abilities.text: Resolve Research and Build in one turn, paying all costs; exhaust both Core Actions and add 2 Scrutiny.
abilities.flavorText: The experiment requires a campus before the hypothesis has finished resolving.
abilities.artDirection: A scientific diagram extruding directly into a colossal construction site.

factions.name: The Vertical Empire
factions.motto: If it can be announced, it can be industrialized.
factions.publicPromise: Compress the path from first principle to planetary infrastructure.
factions.privateAnxiety: Polarization is cheap until Trust becomes a requirement.
factions.introduction: The Vertical Empire treats supply chains, platforms, launch systems, and public attention as one machine. It moves rapidly, builds visibly, and considers terrestrial constraints an invitation to relocate the constraint.
factions.victoryStatement: The future is operational and moving at launch velocity.
factions.artDirection: A severe industrial complex joining factories, rockets, energy systems, and a broadcast tower along one vertical axis.

abilities.name: Industrial Velocity
abilities.text: Cloud or Energy Facilities cost 1 less Runway and add 1 Scrutiny.
abilities.flavorText: The concrete cures while the permit learns to keep up.
abilities.artDirection: A powered facility already operating behind an arriving ribbon-cutting committee.

abilities.name: Move Fast

abilities.flavorText: Distance is reduced through urgency and a highly motivated logistics department.
abilities.artDirection: An executive piece crossing three hexes on the trajectory of a launch vehicle.

abilities.name: Own the Feed
abilities.text: Once per round, choose your result on a two-outcome Headline after other results.
abilities.flavorText: Volatility remains random for organizations without distribution.

abilities.name: Orbital Compute
abilities.text: Move a Facility to any open hex, collect its production, and add 2 Scrutiny.
abilities.flavorText: The cooling plan is mostly night.

factions.name: The Safety Laboratory
factions.motto: Scale only after naming the scale.
factions.publicPromise: Build powerful systems inside explicit, enforceable safety boundaries.
factions.privateAnxiety: A boundary nobody crosses may be indistinguishable from losing.

factions.victoryStatement: The threshold was crossed within the approved framework.

abilities.name: Constitutional Training
abilities.text: Safety-token limit is four.

abilities.artDirection: A model core encircled by a formal illuminated charter.

abilities.name: Responsible Scaling
abilities.text: Once per round, offer a crashed rival one Safety for 1 Runway and gain 1 Trust.
abilities.flavorText: The industry has discovered a market for not making the same mistake twice.

abilities.name: Audited Deployment

abilities.name: Emergency Pause

factions.name: The Foundry
